quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #15
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: When two drivers reach a four-way stop sign at the same time, who goes first?

options.text: The driver on the right.
The driver on the left.
One driver may go without stopping.
One driver should honk to show they are giving up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, if two drivers arrive at the same time, the driver on your right has the right-of-way. You must yield to them. You may go when it is safe.

questions.question: What do drivers need to do on the interstate?

options.text: Be able to safely drive at high speeds.
Stay alert at all times.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Driving safely on the interstate means staying alert and being able to drive at high speeds.

questions.question: Which statement about driving speed is correct?

options.text: Higher speeds increase the chance of death in a crash.
You should increase your following distance when you drive faster.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds greatly increase the risk of death in a crash. At speeds above 80 miles per hour, survival is unlikely. As you drive faster, you need more space behind the car ahead to stop safely.

questions.question: Your blind spot is:

options.text: An area you cannot see without turning your head.
The area directly behind your vehicle.
What you see in your rearview mirror.
What you see in your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: An area you cannot see without turning your head.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas around your vehicle that you cannot see without moving your head. They are found on the sides and behind your car.

questions.question: What helps drivers save gas?

options.text: Leaving the car running in the driveway.
Speeding up quickly.
Slowing down gradually.
Braking suddenly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down gradually.
questions.explanation: Every sudden stop wastes fuel because you have to speed back up. If you look ahead and slow down gradually or change lanes to avoid hard braking, you will use less gas.

questions.question: Looking far ahead while driving on the highway:

options.text: Helps you keep up with traffic.
Reduces the need for sudden braking or turning.
Helps you spot police officers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduces the need for sudden braking or turning.
questions.explanation: By looking far ahead, you can see problems early and stop or change lanes smoothly. This makes driving safer, saves fuel, and helps traffic move steadily.

questions.question: You are on a two-lane road with no bike lane and see a cyclist ahead going the same direction. What is the safest way to pass?

options.text: Slow down and wait for no traffic, then pass while leaving plenty of space.
Keep driving straight. The cyclist must get out of your way.
Wait until you reach a traffic light or stop sign to pass.
Honk to tell the cyclist you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and wait for no traffic, then pass while leaving plenty of space.
questions.explanation: Pass a cyclist like any other vehicle. Leave at least 3 feet of space between your mirror and the cyclist, or 5 feet on faster roads or when there are multiple cyclists. Do not honk—it may startle them and cause a crash.

questions.question: Crashes are more likely when:

options.text: All vehicles travel at about the same speed.
One lane travels faster than other lanes.
One vehicle travels faster or slower than other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: One vehicle travels faster or slower than other traffic.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen more often when one driver goes faster or slower than the other cars. Speeding increases crash risk. Driving too slowly is also dangerous because it can cause rear-end collisions or make other drivers swerve.

questions.question: When weather or darkness requires you to use lights while driving, use:

options.text: Parking lights.
High beams.
Low beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, or rain. High beam light reflects back and creates glare, making it harder to see.

questions.question: A broken yellow line in the center of the road means:

options.text: Passing is not allowed.
You can pass on the right when it is safe.
You can pass on the left when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line on your side means you may cross it to pass another vehicle from the left when the road ahead is clear.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Cars in the right lane must slow down.
No left turn.
Merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign tells drivers that traffic may merge from the right. Be ready to let other vehicles merge safely.

questions.question: Which statement is correct?

options.text: Use your left foot to brake.
Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
Always brake hard to ensure you stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
questions.explanation: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating. Apply the brakes gently with steady pressure so your vehicle stops smoothly.

questions.question: On a green arrow, you must:

options.text: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
Yield to pedestrians only in the intersection.
Wait four seconds before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go. Turn in the direction of the arrow after you yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Bicycle crossing.
Stop only if other cars are approaching.
Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bicycle crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns drivers that bicycles may cross the road ahead.

questions.question: Two solid yellow lines on the road mean:

options.text: Passing is allowed for drivers from both directions.
Passing is not allowed.
Passing is allowed if you are at the top of a hill.
Passing is allowed during daylight only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mean traffic on the other side is moving toward you. Never cross two solid yellow lines to pass from either direction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow-moving vehicle.
Road construction or maintenance area.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle.
questions.explanation: This sign is placed on slow-moving vehicles to warn other drivers.

questions.question: Hard braking on ice and snow often:

options.text: Helps you stop faster.
Locks the front wheels, causing loss of steering control.
Keeps the brakes from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Locks the front wheels, causing loss of steering control.
questions.explanation: Hard braking on snow and ice can lock the front wheels, causing you to lose steering control. Reduce your speed to avoid hard braking.

questions.question: This red and white sign means you should:

options.text: Stop and check for traffic from both directions before proceeding.
Let traffic on the road you want to enter or cross go first.
Keep a steady speed and check for traffic from all directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let traffic on the road you want to enter or cross go first.
questions.explanation: A yield sign tells you to slow down and be ready to stop if needed. Let any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians pass before you proceed. You do not have the right-of-way.

questions.question: If traffic lights are not working due to a power outage:

options.text: Park your vehicle off the road and wait for power to return.
Use hand signals to tell other drivers your plans.
Turn on hazard lights and drive through without stopping.
Treat the intersection as a four-way stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat the intersection as a four-way stop.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is not working, treat the intersection as a four-way stop. Yield to other drivers like you would at a four-way stop, then proceed carefully when it is your turn.

questions.question: Using a cell phone while driving is dangerous because:

options.text: It makes you worry about the cost of the call.
It takes up your hands, eyes, and mind.
It distracts other drivers on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes up your hands, eyes, and mind.
questions.explanation: Cell phones are dangerous while driving because they occupy your eyes, hands, and mind. Even skilled drivers increase their crash risk when using a cell phone.

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line in the center of the road mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed only from your direction.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: A double yellow line means no vehicle can cross it to pass, no matter which direction you are traveling.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in rain?

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
No lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when it is raining.

questions.question: When should you return to your original lane after passing another vehicle?

options.text: When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
When you have cleared the front bumper of the passed vehicle.
When you are 50 feet in front of the passed vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Return to your original lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. This gives you enough safe space between the vehicles.

questions.question: Which lane should you be in to make a left turn from a one-way street?

options.text: The lane nearest the left curb.
The lane nearest the center of the street.
The lane nearest the right curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane nearest the left curb.
questions.explanation: For a left turn, be in the lane closest to the left curb. This allows you to turn into the first available legal lane.

questions.question: When should you use your horn?

options.text: When traveling through an intersection.
When passing a bicyclist.
When you see a child about to run into the street.
When parallel parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see a child about to run into the street.
questions.explanation: Use your horn as a warning when another driver or pedestrian may not see you. For example, use it if a child is about to run in front of your vehicle.

questions.question: When should you not enter an intersection if the light will turn red while you are crossing?

options.text: Under any circumstances.
Unless you entered on a yellow light.
Unless you entered on a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under any circumstances.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection unless you can cross it completely before the light turns red. Even if the light is green, blocking the intersection can result in a citation.

questions.question: Why should you keep your signal on while turning?

options.text: It is illegal to turn off your signal before finishing a turn.
It tells other drivers what you plan to do.
It is always unsafe to turn off a signal before finishing a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: It tells other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Signal when turning, changing lanes, slowing down, or stopping. This tells other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians what you are going to do.

questions.question: What is the correct order of traffic lights from top to bottom?

options.text: Red, yellow, green.
Red, green, yellow.
Green, red, yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Red, yellow, green.
questions.explanation: Traffic lights are ordered from top to bottom as red, yellow, and green. Red is always on top, yellow in the middle, and green on the bottom.

questions.question: What must other drivers consider when driving near heavy trucks?

options.text: Heavy trucks need more distance to stop.
Heavy trucks need less distance to stop.
Heavy trucks make less noise.
Heavy trucks travel faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Heavy trucks need more distance to stop.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles need more time and space to stop. Stay where the truck driver can see you, and do not block their view of the road.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in bad weather?

options.text: Steer off the road.
Drive in a low gear.
Steer and brake smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer and brake smoothly.
questions.explanation: In bad weather, avoid sudden braking and sharp turns. Smooth steering and braking help you keep control of your vehicle.

questions.question: Can you drive off the road to pass another vehicle?

options.text: Yes, if the vehicle ahead is turning left.
Yes, if there are two or more lanes in your direction.
No, never.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: You must never drive off the road or onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line between traffic mean?

options.text: You may pass if it is safe to do so.
Both lanes travel in the same direction.
You may not pass.
You may pass, even if it is dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may pass if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A single dashed yellow line means traffic moves in opposite directions. You can pass if it is safe and you will not interfere with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Use cruise control near a railroad crossing to keep a steady speed.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign tells you to.
You have the right-of-way at a railroad crossing and do not need to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign tells you to.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal. Always be careful near railroad tracks.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: You cannot turn in that direction.
You may turn in that direction after stopping completely.
You may turn in that direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn in that direction.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means you cannot turn in that direction. You must stop and wait for a green light.

questions.question: Must you always stop for a stopped school bus on a two-lane road?

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: TRUE
questions.explanation: You must always stop for a stopped school bus on a two-lane road, no matter which direction you are traveling. Be careful around children.
